turn_text: This is the Missouri Military Minute.

I'm Ashley Byrd. Congress passed the 2022 National Defense Authorization Act. Senator Josh Hawley serves on the Orange Services Committee and made sure the bill included some changes to military justice, taking some prosecution decisions out of the hands of ranking officers.

And both for those who have been victims of the crime, military service members who are victims. But frankly, also for those who have been accused, I think we need to professionalize this process and make sure that our service members are getting the best prosecution as victims that they deserve and then also as their defendants, they're getting a quality defense. So I was disappointed that the Defense Department weakened and watered down these provisions, but I think there was a step forward here when it comes to sexual assault crimes in particular. Those are going to get a new focus. Those are going to get to professionalize the prosecution now in a new way that will be outside of the chain of command. And I think that's important.
